newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Emotional return home for Romania's king.
newsitem.headline: Emotional return home for Romania's king.

text.p: Romania's exiled King Michael, tears streaming down his face, arrived in his homeland on Friday for a five-day visit a week after the new centrist government restored his citizenship.
The king was visibly shaken as he stepped down from a commercial aircraft at Bucharest's Otopeni airport to be mobbed on the tarmac by a crowd of several hundred well-wishers.

Michael, 75, was handed a new Romanian passport by an unidentified official and then made his way to a waiting car, a small bouquet in his hand. Several politicians, including Finance Minister Mircea Ciumara, were present alongside prominent cultural figures.
Well-wishers chanted "The monarchy will save Romania!" and "King Michael, King Michael!". A large portrait of the king, forced to abdicate by pro-Moscow communists in 1947, was carried aloft.

The king's visit is described as private, but President Emil Constantinescu has said he hopes to make use of the monarch's prestige to further Romania's longshot bid for early NATO entry. He is due to meet both Constantinescu and Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea.

The king, who lives in Switzerland, has promised to respect the 1991 constitution which defines Romania as a presidential republic and make no claims for restitution of property seized by the communists. He first returned to Romania in 1992 to be met by vast crowds but a subsequent visit was blocked by leftists thrown out of office last November.
